prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
**Goal** — Win95 archery level 1 in `./game/index.html`, single file, playable in browser with only Google Fonts reachable.

**Assumptions I chose** (brief left them open): level 1 = pop 10 of drifting balloons within 15 arrows; lose = out of arrows with none in flight; win screen on 10 pops; power = hold duration (0.9 s to full draw, tremble at full power); all audio synthesized via WebAudio (no files, works on `file://`); Win95 chrome drawn in CSS + canvas, "Press Start 2P" from Google Fonts with monospace fallback.

**Action/Result** — `game/index.html` delivered (canvas game: Win95 window frame, teal desktop, pixel archer with draw-back bow, trajectory preview dots, color-coded power meter, balloons with bob/tilt, pop particles + ring + screen shake, floating +10, Win95 beveled HUD plates, menu/lose/win panels). Sounds: whoosh+plunk on shoot, noise-snap+chirp on pop, dud click on weak release, UI blip, lose descent, win arpeggio.

Verified in-browser by dispatching pointer events and reading game state:
- Menu screenshot: title panel + START button rendered correctly.
- `pointerdown/up` on menu → `{mode:"play"}`.
- Firing → arrow counter 15→14, then 14→13 (shots register, power ramp works).
- Pinned balloon, full-power shot → `{score:10, arrows:12}` (pop + scoring + collision verified).
- Forced last arrow into empty sky → after arrow exits, `{mode:"over"}` (lose path verified; win path is the same branch on `popped>=10`).

Open tabs closed. I could not hear the audio (no audio capture in the test harness), but the WebAudio graphs are standard and the context resumes on first click; the only limit is that sound quality is unverified by ear.

**Next** — nothing; open `game/index.html` and play.
